reconcile.connective: Harmonizers read 15:35 as Samuel ceasing to seek Saul out, not denying that Saul later came before him in 19:24.

discrepancy.connective: Henry Preserved Smith renders 15:35 "Samuel saw Saul no more till the day of his death" and holds that the plain sense flatly contradicts the encounter narrated in 19:24.

skeptic.name: Henry Preserved Smith
skeptic.work: A Critical and Exegetical Commentary on the Books of Samuel (International Critical Commentary)
skeptic.attribution: Henry Preserved Smith (d. 1927), A Critical and Exegetical Commentary on the Books of Samuel, ICC (1899)

excerpts.excerpt_text: not that he saw him no more, he saw him afterwards, Sa1 19:24, but it was accidentally, he did not go to see him, but Saul came to him …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly names the apparent conflict (15:35 vs 19:24) and resolves it on the mechanism the harmonizers all use: Samuel did not go to Saul; Saul came to Samuel. Strongest single reconcile, parity-capped at 1 to match the discrepancy pole's named-skeptic count.

pd_work.resource: Adam Clarke, Commentary on the Bible (1832), at 1 Samuel 15:35
pd_work.author: Adam Clarke
pd_work.note: Clarke addresses this exact discrepancy on the passage: he grants that Saul went to Samuel at Naioth (19:22-24) but argues this does not affect 15:35, since from that time Samuel had no further connection with Saul as king.
